title: Truveon roster
description: Questionnaire section 16.5: the people who get accounts in the client's Truveon tenant. A sidecar for the same reason as the developer roster (vesting/roster.schema.json) -- it is nothing but personal data, and the questionnaire schema and its committed example must not be able to reach it. Real ones are named <client>.truveon.roster.yaml, live in completed_qs/, and are blocked from commit by .gitignore and the pre-commit hook. A different list from the developer roster on purpose: the people who read compliance evidence are rarely the people who deploy the application, and deriving one from the other would give developers GRC access nobody asked for.

tenant.description: Repeated from the questionnaire so the roster names the tenant it grants access to. truveon-tenant-handoff.sh refuses to proceed unless both match the questionnaire exactly. Per client, with no application code: the Truveon tenant is per client (B-023).

users.description: One entry per person. Exactly one must be the owner when the tenant is being created; for an existing tenant the owner already exists and none is required.

role.description: Truveon membership role. Free text in Truveon today (tenant_memberships.role; persona-level roles are unscoped work there), so this is not an enum here either -- an enum on this side would claim a control Truveon does not enforce. Defaults to 'contributor'; the owner's defaults to 'admin'.

is_global_admin.description: Tenant-wide administration in Truveon. Forced true for the owner.

owner.description: The tenant's first Owner (Truveon's identity design, Mode A). A separate decision from the rest of the list, and Truveon takes it as a separate argument.
